chunk_findings.detail: Correction runs only on the item being claimed (`want` / `claimed`), then that item’s globs are leased. It never rewrites other open items, and there is no split-time rewrite or batch command. Given open T-other still declaring `ddflow/config.py` and T-this claiming (and being rewritten to) `ddflow/config/`, overlap still compares a lease of `ddflow/config/` with a stored glob of `ddflow/config.py`, which covers none of `ddflow/config/_core.py`. The two tasks still cannot see each other — the failure B-stale-globs-after-split-wave describes — until every other stale item happens to be claimed.

chunk_findings.detail: The helper computes `corrected` but the caller only stores it in the local `want`; it never writes it back to `claimed.globs` or includes it in the persisted item updates. The later persistence call `OG.claim_fields(st, cfg, item, repo)` at line 314 is not passed `want`, so an open item such as `ADP-config-store` declaring `ddflow/config.py` will have its lease globs corrected to `ddflow/config` but the stored item will still declare `ddflow/config.py`, leaving the stale open item to be hit again on the next claim. This contradicts the docstring’s “the lease and the item both take the package path” and the bug intent that claim corrects the stale package glob.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py:271 (_correct_stale_package_globs)

chunk_findings.detail: `_apply_stale_globs` only rewrites item records via `_items.update`; it never breaks or retargets active leases. In the motivating case, an open item such as `GR-prompt-guard` is held with a live lease on `ddflow/config.py`. Running `ddflow doctor --fix-stale-globs` as the doctor runner passes that runner's `agent` to `_items.update`, but that agent is not the holder. If `_items.update` enforces the lease, it returns a lease conflict; if it does not, the item spec changes while the active lease still resolves to the old module path. Either way the holder's lease is not retargeted to `ddflow/config/`, so two tasks editing `ddflow/config/_core.py` still cannot see each other. This contradicts the function’s own docstring (“each holder’s lease is retargeted”) and leaves the live-lease side of B-stale-globs-after-split-wave unfixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:_apply_stale_globs

chunk_findings.detail: `--fix-stale-globs` rewrites the shared item registry from `W.git_paths(repo, "ls-files")`, i.e. the current index, not the tree the bug measures (`git ls-tree main`). On a branch or dirty index that has split `api/setup.py` into `api/setup/` while main still has the module, every open item that declares `api/setup.py` is rewritten to the package path. Those tasks then lease a path that does not exist on main and no longer cover `api/setup.py`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:_apply_stale_globs

chunk_findings.detail: A rejected rewrite is only appended to `notes` (`"{id}: stale globs not corrected: ..."`), and `health` does `notes += _stale_glob_section(...)` with no `problems` entry. If `items.update` returns non-OK (locked item, agent rejected), doctor still exits success, so a caller treating exit 0 as “globs rewritten” leaves the stale `*.py` declarations in place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:_apply_stale_globs

chunk_findings.detail: When `ddflow doctor --fix-stale-globs` cannot apply the requested fix, the failure is placed in `notes`, not `problems`. `_apply_stale_globs` returns `"stale task globs not fixed: git could not list the tracked files"` when `tracked is None`, and it emits `"stale globs not corrected: ..."` when `_items.update` returns a non-`OK` outcome. The call site (`notes += _stale_glob_section(...)`) adds all of this to the doctor note list, so the failure is not represented as a doctor problem. For example, if `git ls-files` fails or one item update is rejected, the command can finish with a success status even though the stale globs are still uncorrected, leaving the 288 open items exactly in the broken state this change is meant to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py `_apply_stale_globs`

chunk_findings.detail: `_apply_stale_globs` attempts to extract `globs_withheld` from `out.data` and report withheld globs if present. However, `_items.update` does not return a `globs_withheld` field in its outcome data when active leases prevent updating certain globs. Consequently, any withheld globs during `ddflow doctor --fix-stale-globs` are silently ignored and never reported in the notes, misleading the user into thinking the globs were fully corrected when they were not.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `withheld` branch appends to `notes` but not to `problems`. The change’s own contract says “A stale glob the fix could not rewrite is a PROBLEM”; a non-empty `globs_withheld` is exactly a stale glob not rewritten because a live lease held by a different agent prevented the item record from being corrected. Given `GR-prompt-guard` held by another agent on `ddflow/config.py`, `_items.update` returns OK with `globs_withheld=['ddflow/config.py']`: the open item still declares the stale module glob, so two tasks editing `ddflow/config/_core.py` still cannot see each other, yet `ddflow doctor --fix-stale-globs` reports no problem for that item. The earlier refutation probe for finding 2 only ran the no-withheld success test, so it does not answer this path.

chunk_findings.detail: The no-`.py` short-circuit was moved into `stale_glob_updates`, but `stale_glob_notes` now calls `W.git_paths(repo, "ls-files")` before that short-circuit runs. In a repository whose unfinished items have no glob ending in `.py` and where `git ls-files` fails (`W.git_paths` returns `None`), the old code returned `[]` without touching git; the new code instead returns `["stale task globs not checked: git could not list the tracked files"]`. Since no item can have a stale `.py` package glob in that state, this is a spurious doctor note caused by the refactor.

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier probe does not answer this: sharing `W.git_paths(repo, "ls-files")` with doctor notes is not the same as rewriting the shared registry, and "doctor runs on primary == main" is false for a dirty index. Given main still has `api/setup.py` (the tree the bug measures with `git ls-tree main`) while the index has staged the split to `api/setup/`, `--fix-stale-globs` rewrites every open item that declares `api/setup.py` onto `api/setup/`. Those items then lease a path that does not exist on main and no longer cover `api/setup.py`, so overlap with tasks still on the module is invisible. The same `ls-files` source is now used by the new `_correct_stale_package_globs` in `ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py`, so a claim from that index persists the same wrong retarget.

chunk_findings.detail: The new claim-time correction uses `W.git_paths(repo, "ls-files")`, i.e. the current worktree’s index, not the tree the bug measures (`git ls-tree main`). The earlier HIGH against `health.py` was refuted only because doctor runs on the primary checkout/main tree; claim has no such invariant: `claim` runs in the repository/working tree the agent is currently in. Concrete failure: an agent claims from a feature branch created before a split, where `api/setup.py` still exists and `api/setup/` does not, while `main` has `api/setup/`. An open item declares `api/setup.py` (stale against main). `tracked` from that branch contains `api/setup.py` and no `api/setup/_core.py`, so `stale_package_globs` returns no stale result, `_correct_stale_package_globs` returns `want` unchanged, and `lz.globs` remains `api/setup.py`. The lease then covers none of `api/setup/` on main, so overlapping edits to `api/setup/_core.py` remain invisible. The correction should be based on the main tree for open-item globs, not the local index.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py:184 `_correct_stale_package_globs`

chunk_findings.detail: The fix rewrites the shared item registry from `W.git_paths(repo, "ls-files")`, i.e. the current index of `repo`, not the `git ls-tree main` tree the bug is measured against. `health()` accepts an arbitrary `repo` and never pins it to `main`; on a branch or dirty/staged index that has split `api/setup.py` into `api/setup/` while `main` still has the module, every open item declaring `api/setup.py` is rewritten to `api/setup/` and loses its lease on the file that still exists on `main`. The previous triage says doctor runs on the primary checkout and thus `ls-files` equals `main`, but nothing in this code enforces that, and the new mutation makes the wrong-tree choice destructive rather than merely cosmetic.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:_apply_stale_globs

chunk_findings.detail: When `_items.update` returns `O.OK` but with nonempty `globs_withheld`, the requested rewrite is only partly applied, yet `_apply_stale_globs` appends a `notes` entry instead of a `problems` entry. The section's own contract says a stale glob the fix could not rewrite is a PROBLEM. A `ddflow doctor --fix-stale-globs` run can therefore exit successfully while an item remains only "partly corrected" and still has a stale package glob withheld, so a caller treating exit 0 as "all stale globs were rewritten" is wrong. Example: another live lease prevents the replacement package glob from being added; the code records `"globs partly corrected; withheld: ..."` and returns no problem.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:_apply_stale_globs
